tagline: From river towns to a lake once targeted for drainage
intro: Pamlico Scenic Byway is among the coastal-plain routes in North Carolina’s scenic-byways guide. Water shapes its towns: Washington occupies the Pamlico River’s north bank, while Belhaven stands on the north shore of the Pungo River.

At Lake Mattamuskeet, investors and a public drainage district tried to turn water into land between 1911 and 1934. They built a pumping plant and dredged canals for development, creating New Holland within the reclaimed lakebed. The project ended with a 1934 sale to the federal government for a migratory bird refuge.

From Washington and Bath, the eastward sequence includes Belhaven and Scranton on US 264, northwest of Swan Quarter. Mattamuskeet refuge lies east of Swan Quarter; farther east, Engelhard is a fishing community at the head of Far Creek. Manns Harbor sits on Croatan Sound, east of the junction of US 64 and US 264.

moments.title: Bath
moments.text: Main Street borders the waterfront lots that John Lawson laid out for Bath, where water was the principal transportation route. Lawson helped secure the 1705 charter for North Carolina’s first town and port of entry. Merchants traded naval stores, furs and tobacco. Blackbeard settled here in 1718 after receiving a royal pardon, then returned to piracy that same year. The town lies almost entirely within Lawson’s original boundaries. Its importance as a port and government center later declined as nearby New Bern grew, leaving a town whose population has never exceeded 400.

moments.title: Lake Mattamuskeet
moments.text: North Carolina’s largest natural lake averages only two to three feet deep, despite stretching 18 miles long and seven miles wide. The attempt to drain it left a brick pumping station built in 1911. The pumping station’s three-story brick body is connected to a tower rising 120 feet. After the federal acquisition in 1934, that building was remodeled as refuge headquarters and visitor lodging. The lake and old New Holland townsite are now within Mattamuskeet National Wildlife Refuge. The refuge and surrounding lands provide wintering habitat for northern pintails, green-wing teal, Canada geese and tundra swans.

moments.title: Alligator River National Wildlife Refuge
moments.text: Restoring water levels is part of the work at Alligator River National Wildlife Refuge. Its management objectives include plugging artificial drainage ditches to reduce fire danger and restore wildlife habitat. Established in 1984 to protect pocosin wetland habitat, the refuge also contains hardwood swamps, bogs, and fresh and brackish marshes. Its wildlife includes red wolves, red-cockaded woodpeckers and alligators. The refuge’s boundaries also contain the Dare County Bombing Range. Pond pine, Atlantic white cypress and red maple grow here, alongside pitcher plants and sundews, among the refuge’s varied wetland plant communities.
